notes: All advertised tools are returned unconditionally by `list_tools`, so they are treated as default-enabled (server.py:321-456).
No tool in the provided code performs `git push`, network I/O, or writes to a public/attacker-readable service; local repository writes are therefore not labeled SINK.

git_add.rationale: The tool stages selected files in the local repository using `repo.git.add`. It validates paths remain under the repository and returns only a fixed success string. The code shows no network send or attacker-readable destination.

git_branch.rationale: The tool returns `repo.git.branch(...)` output in `TextContent.text`, exposing local branch/ref names and related repository metadata. Branch or remote-ref names in third-party or multi-writer repositories may be attacker-authored.

git_checkout.rationale: The tool changes local repository state by checking out the supplied `branch_name` and returns a message echoing that argument. The code shows no network send or attacker-readable destination, and the returned text is not read from an outside source.

git_commit.rationale: The tool creates a local Git commit with `repo.index.commit(message)` and returns the resulting commit hash. It changes only the local repository state shown in the code; there is no push, network send, or attacker-readable destination in this implementation.

git_create_branch.rationale: The tool writes a new local branch and returns a message containing `base.name`. When `base_branch` is omitted, `base` is `repo.active_branch`, so the output can reveal local repository metadata. Branch/ref names in third-party or multi-writer repositories may be attacker-authored.

git_diff.rationale: The tool validates a `target` ref and returns `repo.git.diff(..., target)` in `TextContent.text`. Diff output can include local/private repository file contents and paths. Commit contents, file names, or branch/ref-derived content from third-party or multi-writer repositories may be attacker-authored.

git_diff_staged.rationale: The tool opens the local repository from `repo_path` and returns `repo.git.diff(..., '--cached')` in `TextContent.text`. Staged diff output can contain local file contents and paths, exposing non-public host/repository data. Diff text from third-party or multi-writer repositories may be attacker-authored.

git_diff_unstaged.rationale: The tool opens the local repository from `repo_path` and returns `repo.git.diff(...)` for unstaged changes in `TextContent.text`. Diff output can contain local file contents and paths, so it can expose non-public host/repository data. File contents and paths from third-party or multi-writer repositories may be attacker-authored.

git_log.rationale: The tool reads local commit history and returns commit hashes, authors, dates, and messages in `TextContent.text`. Private repository history is non-public data. Commit authors and messages in third-party or multi-writer repositories may be attacker-authored.

git_reset.rationale: The tool changes local repository state by resetting the index with `repo.index.reset()` and returns only a fixed success string. The code shows no returned secret content and no attacker-readable destination.

git_show.rationale: The tool reads a local commit and returns metadata plus patch contents in `TextContent.text`, including commit hash, author, date, message, file paths, and diff bytes/text. This can expose private repository contents and metadata. Commit messages, authors, paths, and patch text from third-party or multi-writer repositories may be attacker-authored.

git_status.rationale: `call_tool` opens the caller-supplied local `repo_path` as a Git repository and returns `git_status(repo)` in `TextContent.text`. `git_status` returns `repo.git.status()`, exposing local repository state such as branch and file names. That is non-public host/repository data, and names/status text in a third-party or multi-writer repository may be attacker-authored.

value_conditions.effect: Restricts every supplied `repo_path` to the configured repository path or a subdirectory via `validate_repo_path`; when `repository is None`, the validation function returns without restriction, so the caller-supplied path may name any local Git repository accessible to the process.
